description: Deterministic, single-threaded tick-simulation parameters shared byte-for-byte between the Java and Rust suites. Every dataset's production schedule includes a long trailing all-drain tail so the consumer always fully empties the queue by the end of the simulation — this is what lets the correctness invariant (produced == delivered + rejected + dropped + superseded) hold exactly, with no 'still queued at end' remainder to reconcile. The real concurrent wall-clock timing question this lab teaches is answered separately by the JMH/Criterion benchmark harness, not by this deterministic fixture.

steadyBelowCapacity.note: Producer rate equals consumer rate; the queue should never grow past a handful of items for any bounded policy, and the unbounded policy should behave identically to the bounded ones here (no overload to distinguish them).

shortBurst.note: A short burst well above capacity (20/tick vs a consume rate of 4/tick and capacity 8), followed by a long drain-only tail so every policy fully recovers.

sustainedOverload.note: Sustained overload (10/tick vs consume rate 4/tick) for long enough that bounded policies must reject/drop/coalesce repeatedly, not just once.

hotKeySkew.note: Same overload shape as sustainedOverload, but a much smaller key space (3 keys) so COALESCE_BY_KEY has heavy repeated-key collisions to collapse.

correctnessInvariant: produced == delivered + rejected + dropped + superseded, for every (policy, dataset) pair, with zero items left queued at the end of the simulation.
